title: Texas's 18th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for Texas's 18th Congressional District pits Democratic incumbent Rep. Christian Menefee against Republican nominee Ronald Whitfield. The district was significantly redrawn by the Republican-controlled Texas legislature in 2025, forcing an incumbent-on-incumbent Democratic primary between Menefee and longtime Rep. Al Green, which Menefee won on May 26, 2026. The newly configured 18th District encompasses parts of southwest, central, and northeast Houston and remains heavily Democratic with a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+29. Menefee, a freshman congressman who previously served as Harris County Attorney, is heavily favored to win the general election in this deep-blue district.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the general election matchup between Christian Menefee and Ronald Whitfield in Texas's 18th Congressional District. The district is rated 'Solid D' by the Cook Political Report with a PVI of D+29.

candidates.name: Christian Menefee
candidates.summary: Christian Menefee is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 18th Congressional District, first sworn in on February 2, 2026 after winning a special election. He previously served as Harris County Attorney from 2021 to 2026, where he was the youngest person and first African American to hold that office. Menefee, an attorney and former commercial litigator, defeated fellow Democratic incumbent Al Green in a May 2026 primary runoff after mid-decade redistricting forced them into the same district.

candidates.summary: Ronald Dwayne Whitfield is the Republican nominee for U.S. House in Texas's 18th Congressional District, having won the Republican primary on March 3, 2026. He is a perennial candidate who previously ran in the November 2025 special election for the same seat. Very little biographical information is publicly available about Whitfield, who did not respond to candidate questionnaires from local media outlets.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polls exist for this race, which reduces precision but does not alter the fundamental structural picture. The district's Cook PVI is D+29, it is rated Solid D by the Cook Political Report, and the Democratic incumbent Christian Menefee faces a Republican challenger, Ronald Whitfield, described as a perennial candidate with little public profile and no reported fundraising or campaign infrastructure. Mid-decade redistricting forced a competitive Democratic primary (Menefee defeated longtime incumbent Al Green), but the general-election configuration remains overwhelmingly Democratic. With no polling available, the forecast relies entirely on these structural factors: the district's deep-blue partisan lean, Menefee's incumbency, and Whitfield's apparent lack of campaign resources. A very high Democratic win probability is warranted, though the absence of polling data caps confidence at medium.
